pr_title: Fix PKCS12_newpass() to work with PBES2.
pr_body:
Fixes #19092

The code looks like it was written to work with PBES1. As it had no tests, this would of then broken when PBES2 was introduced at a later point.

Also added libctx and propq support.

This affects the shroudedkeybag object.

issue_context.title: Bug with PKCS12_newpass
comments:
Hello

I thought that there was more reactivity on this project
Nobody has problem with this function ?

Regards
Gilles

Looking at the actual code it uses internally indicates that there is little chance that this would work without some major changes. There is absolutely NO tests for this API and it only looks for PBEPARAM inside a function called alg_get(). If you have scrypt or more commonly PBES2 then it will fail.. This is not a regression, it has been broken for a very long time.

Hello
Your response is very curious. I just take the sample in manpage of openssl 3.0 (https://www.openssl.org/docs/man3.0/man3/PKCS12_newpass.html) (and also 3.1)
So it isn't an old API, but a supported API.
I just use the sample in manpage, not more.
Otherwise, how can we change password of .p12 file in C ?

Regards
Gilles

Hello

I tested again the fix, and the modification of password is not possible.
Do you have another fix ?

Regards
Gilles

If the file contains only one private key and corresponding certificate chain, you can extract them using `PKCS12_parse()` and then recreate with `PKCS12_create()` passing the new password. 
With OpenSSL 3.0 it would be necessary to load the legacy provider if the input file is encrypted by outdated algorithms.
